meta.topic: ThreeUI (MengTo/threeui) research for geneyu.me: (1) feasibility + plan for a custom Three.js hero scene inspired by 'Sylva', (2) options for a more distinctive projects/works showcase than the current grid+modal
meta.purpose: Durable, updatable record of all ThreeUI research (hero scene + projects showcase), the options considered, and phased plans, so work can resume in a new session without re-deriving anything.
meta.lastUpdated: 2026-09-16 - added projectsShowcaseOptions section; no implementation started on either topic

trigger.what: Gene saw threeui.com's 'Sylva' hero component (paywalled 'Get Pro' catalog entry) - a living-world Three.js forest scene with local Lexend type, card imagery, and two native liquid-metal controls - and asked whether something similar could be built for geneyu.me's hero.
trigger.sylvaPageUrl: not captured - Gene pasted the catalog card text, no URL was given; do not guess one

repo.name: MengTo/threeui
repo.license: MIT for app code, Community component code, and ThreeUI-authored Community imagery. Bundled fonts are SIL OFL 1.1. Bundled three.js runtime files are MIT. Remote catalog thumbnails/previews from threeui.com are NOT redistributable.
repo.stack: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite 7, npm package @designcodeio/threeui, peer deps react >=18 <20 / three >=0.149 <1
repo.structure: Pro and Beta components are stripped from this public repo; only Community-tier components ship with source. 50 Community parent components, 141 free variants.

proLayer.status: locked - source NOT available in the public repo
proLayer.contains: full hero page layout, Lexend type pairing, card imagery, page chrome, two 'native' liquid-metal controls integrated into that specific layout, plus 3 derived variants (re-dressed scene + retoned chrome)

communityLayer.sceneSourceSize: 197914 bytes, 4304 lines, single self-contained file (HTML+CSS+JS+bundled three.js r128 runtime as an inlined string)
mountingPattern: Scene is a full standalone HTML document loaded into a sandboxed iframe via srcDoc (sandbox="allow-scripts"), not mounted directly into the host React tree
IntersectionObserver on the host div pauses mounting when off-screen
document.visibilitychange listener pauses when the tab is hidden
prefers-reduced-motion media query swaps in a loop that skips requestAnimationFrame
three.js runtime is inlined as a JS string and injected via a <script> tag inside the iframe doc - it never touches the host page's module graph or bundle
sceneContents: Procedural tree trunk built from CatmullRomCurve3 skeleton + custom bark ShaderMaterial
InstancedBufferGeometry grass/fur and fern instances, each with an independent per-instance quaternion
Flower billboards textured via a canvas-generated CanvasTexture (drawn at runtime, not an image asset)
Pollen/dust particle system (THREE.Points + custom shader), plus a separate spray/burst particle system apparently tied to interaction
Three-light rig (key/fill/ambient) with hand-tuned colors, ACESFilmicToneMapping, sRGB output encoding

A separate liquid-metal button shader (uP[21] tunables, ripple/rim/pointer-well uniforms) mounted via a small IIFE, same raw-WebGL technique discussed earlier for the standalone liquid-metal-button component
communityLayer.assessment: Hand-authored, production-polished, effectively a bespoke small 3D-graphics project (hundreds of hours of work), not a drop-in effect. Densely commented but variable names are heavily abbreviated (uRip, uPtrK, uP[21]) - readable as reference, expensive to maintain if adopted wholesale.

optionsConsidered.name: Directly reuse/recolor the Sylva forest scene
reasons: Thematic mismatch: ferns/flowers/butterfly reads as an eco/nature brand, not 'software engineer, trading systems, AI'
Recoloring only changes the palette, not the silhouette/motion language - still reads as a forest
4304-line file with heavily abbreviated tunables is expensive to safely modify past palette swaps
Much of the interaction code (burst/spray particles) looks tied to that page's specific button placements, dead weight if repurposed

optionsConsidered.name: Borrow Sylva's technical pattern (iframe-sandboxed, self-contained three.js doc, IntersectionObserver + reduced-motion + tab-visibility handling) but design a bespoke, on-theme scene, assembled from the smaller Community components as reference/building blocks
reasons: Candidate components are 1-15KB vs Sylva's 198KB - far less to read, adapt, and maintain
Can pick a concept that actually matches the portfolio narrative (data/constellation network, orbital motion, or a reworked globe)
Mounting pattern (iframe srcDoc isolation) keeps three.js out of the main Vite bundle regardless of which scene is chosen - same benefit without the content mismatch
liquid-form + liquid-metal-button already give a lower-risk parallel path to ship visible progress before the bigger scene decision is finalized

decision.status: confirmed 2026-09-16 (Gene: '試試看囉 反正不行頂多revert'); Phase 0 done, Phase 1+2 implemented locally as src/components/OrbitalSphere.tsx wrapped around the hero portrait - see phases for status
decision.rationale: Portfolio audience is decided as software/AI/trading-systems engineering (see site-audit-2026-09-15.json decisions), so an eco/nature scene works against the positioning regardless of execution quality.

tasks.note: Composition history: v1 concentric particle sphere around the portrait -> '病毒球' + '兩個同心圓不協調'. v3 smooth lit sphere offset up-right -> still '有點噁' (dense speckled surface), but Gene liked the orbits and asked for bold, flat solar-system ellipses spanning half to 2/3 of the page. v4 flat affine ellipses with comet trails -> Gene: '不是純2D旋轉', showed a NASA-style solar-system illustration (sun cropped at the left edge, orbits with strong perspective, shaded 3D planets, Saturn ring, stars). v5 (current, src/components/OrbitalSystem.tsx): a real perspective camera, low and close (elevation 24deg, 7.2 units from the focus, fov 50) so near arcs are big and far arcs small; canvas covers the WHOLE hero section BELOW the content (zIndex 0, no hole shader any more - the portrait simply occludes). Portrait = the sun: its screen centre is mapped to a world point at the focus distance (camera.localToWorld) and the system root moves there; corona sprite + PointLight (intensity 110, decay 2) at the focus light the planets. Six eccentric orbits (a 1.6-4.2, e 0.34-0.40, periapsis 44-68deg so the long side sweeps toward the viewer's lower-left, where the perspective is strongest and the page is empty; Kepler's law makes planets linger there). Planets are MeshStandardMaterial spheres (sizes 0.09-0.24, palette pale/blue/mint/amber/lavender/ice; the amber one has a RingGeometry ring), ACES tone mapping, AmbientLight 0.6, scene.fog toward the page background for depth, 320 twinkling stars far behind, slight pointer parallax on the root. v5.1 after Gene's next round ('傾角左下到右上', planets must pass IN FRONT of the photo, faster): camera rolled -24deg about the view axis so the disc runs lower-left -> upper-right; elevation 32deg, focus distance 8; the PHOTO IS NOW RENDERED INSIDE THE SCENE (CircleGeometry + MeshBasicMaterial with the avatar texture, toneMapped false, rim ring; kept parallel to the image plane via camera.quaternion - lookAt(camera) gave a 10% wide-angle stretch off-axis) at the focus, so depth testing lets near planets/arcs cross in front of it; the DOM portrait fades out on onReady but stays for LCP/alt. Planet speed 0.5*a^-1.5. Periapsis angles (30/22/34/16/20/6 deg) were solved with scratch/orbit-calc.mjs (projects apoapsis to screen px for given camera params) so all six apoapses land on one diagonal in the empty lower-left of a 1440x900 hero - guessing angles by screenshot loops failed three times; use the calc script for any retune. Planet sizes 0.11-0.30. Lessons: elevation 18deg + apoapsis pointed straight at the viewer put every planet below the frame; apoapsis toward the near-right went off the right edge because the portrait is only 290px from it. v5.2 after Gene's next round ('photo shouldn't rotate with the axis, flip it back upright, no tilt needed' + 'want the old jagged/dashed ring back, has tech feel' + 'rotation axis should run lower-right to upper-left, upper-left tilting slightly into the screen' + 'disc too flat, each orbit could use some variation' + 'mobile Work section isn't a left-right swipe carousel'): (1) portrait is now a THREE.Sprite with a canvas-masked circular texture + alphaTest:0.5 (so transparent corners don't write depth and wrongly occlude planets), not a hand-oriented Mesh - a Sprite's billboard math is identical to the old camera.quaternion-copy trick (mathematically already renders upright regardless of camera roll) but removes all custom per-frame orientation code as a source of risk. (2) Restored a DOM/CSS rotating dashed ring (border 1.5px dashed, inset -14, 22s spin) as a permanent zIndex:2 tech-HUD accent above the canvas, alongside the existing fading solid border. (3) Camera ROLL is a rotation, not a reflection - flipping its sign does NOT mirror the composition (verified numerically: roll+24 with negated periapsis actually swapped which orbit end is near/far, the opposite of what was wanted). The fix that actually worked: keep ROLL=-24 and re-solve periapsis (scratch/orbit-calc3.mjs, which reports view-space Z to distinguish near/far, not just screen x/y) targeting apoapsis at small positive relative-x/y (lower-right of the portrait, near in Z) - solved values 73/73/71/69/69/61deg. Constraint found the hard way: the portrait sits near the hero's right edge (~1146 of 1440px), so 'lower-right' has only ~290px of room before the viewport edge - some clipping of the largest orbits (bled off the right/bottom) is expected and matches the reference photo's own cropped-sun framing. (4) Inclination range widened from +-2..4deg to +-7..15deg per orbit (was too small to break the coplanar 'flat disc' read) - re-solving periapsis after this was necessary since inc materially shifts where each orbit's apoapsis lands. (5) ProjectsSection.tsx: removed the isDesktop-gated vertical Tile stack fallback entirely (and the now-fully-unused Tile/Meta components, ~140 lines) - the Filmstrip/StageCard now renders on ALL viewport sizes via a per-breakpoint CARD_W (xs 'clamp(240px,78vw,380px)', sm 'clamp(380px,55vw,460px)', md unchanged), with xs padding/font-size added to StageCard's content block (previously md-only, so mobile had zero padding and oversized default h4 text). Verified: real touch-simulated swipe (Puppeteer touchscreen) on a 390px viewport moved scrollLeft 0->328 and correctly centred the next card. All uncommitted, awaiting Gene's verdict.
tasks.openIssue: Numeric check (not yet screenshot-confirmed as a problem, just noted from the solved geometry): periapsis - the point that passes closest to the portrait on screen - is very slightly FARTHER in view-space Z (~-8.9) than the portrait's own depth (~-8), so strictly by the numbers the portrait would occlude a planet passing near it, not the reverse, even though apoapsis (which IS nearer, ~-4 to -6) never gets close enough in screen-XY to visibly overlap. If Gene reports planets still don't appear to cross in front of the photo, the fix is to nudge the portrait's placement very slightly farther from camera than periapsis's closest approach (or accept it - the effect may already read fine given how thin the overlap window is).
tasks.v5.3: Same session, immediately after: Gene sent a reference photo (classic NASA solar-system diagram: sun cropped at the frame edge, orbits as tight nested arcs hugging the sun on the near side and sweeping up/away on the far side, planets growing dramatically bigger as their orbit widens) and said 'the planet angle still isn't right, I want THIS angle' - v5.2's ±7-15deg inclination scatter was the wrong lever; the reference's 3D read comes from a very SHALLOW/near-edge-on ELEVATION producing strong perspective foreshortening (near arcs big and low, far arcs tiny and high), not from crossing orbital planes. Changes: ELEVATION dropped 32deg -> 14deg; inclination scatter walked back down to a small +-3..4deg (just enough to keep lines from perfectly overlapping, not a structural feature); eccentricity raised 0.34-0.40 -> 0.40-0.48 for a more dramatic near/far asymmetry; periapsis angles reset to a near-uniform ~60-67deg band (was individually solved 61-73deg) so all six orbits curve the SAME direction as one consistent nested fan rather than each pointing a slightly different way. Also: dashed tech ring pulled in from inset -14 to -8 (Gene: 'closer to the portrait, like the old geneyu.me build'); removed the redundant hero-body 'Resume' button (Gene: header nav already has a Download Resume button) - DownloadIcon import removed as it's now unused in HeroSection.tsx. Screenshot-verified the nested-arc read at both 1440x900 and 390x828.
tasks.v5.4: Same session, next round: Gene asked for the disc bigger/near full-bleed and a much more obvious speed differential between inner and outer planets. FOCUS_DISTANCE 8->6.4 (camera moved closer) and every orbit's `a` scaled ~1.6x (2.1-6.9, was 1.3-4.3) with `size` scaled to match - peri/e are ratios and scale-invariant so the already-solved nested-arc orientation carried over unchanged, just bigger; orbit arcs now sweep across most of the viewport and bleed off multiple edges. Speed exponent changed from the real-Kepler a^-1.5 to an exaggerated a^-2.3 (coefficient 0.9), widening the innermost/outermost angular-speed ratio from ~6x to ~15x so the difference reads at a glance instead of needing a stopwatch.
tasks.v5.5: Same session, next round, two independent asks: (1) restore the original connecting-dots background ('geneyu.me本來的那個connecting dots'). ParticleNetwork.tsx had been rm'd but never committed as deleted, so `git checkout -- src/components/ParticleNetwork.tsx` recovered it byte-for-byte; re-added to HeroSection.tsx as the bottom-most layer (renders before the OrbitalSystem Box in DOM order, no explicit z-index needed) so it reads as a distant starfield behind the solar system. (2) 'the orbit centre isn't really the portrait, feels off - shift the whole thing up-left, don't touch the angles.' Root cause: Kepler ellipses have their FOCUS (where the portrait sits) offset from the ellipse's own visual centre toward periapsis - the apoapsis-heavy solved geometry bulges its visual mass away from the portrait, so the portrait reads as sitting at the edge of the cluster rather than in it. Fix, without touching ELEVATION/ROLL/peri/inc (which Gene explicitly said not to touch): added a `discRoot` group, child of `root`, that carries ONLY the orbit `frame`s (NOT the corona/sun light, which must stay exactly on the portrait) - offset from root by a small screen-space delta computed the same way as the portrait-anchor projection (camera.localToWorld of an intentionally-offset screen point, minus root.position, giving a root-local delta since root itself carries no persistent rotation). First attempt used a fixed pixel offset (-190,-260) tuned on desktop and it swung a planet straight onto the headline text on mobile's much smaller viewport; fixed by expressing the offset as a RATIO of the portrait's own on-screen width (-0.233, -0.317) instead of fixed px, recomputed in syncAnchor every resize - same visual proportion at every breakpoint. Screenshot-verified at both sizes: portrait now sits inside the arc cluster with a planet visibly passing close by it, no text overlap on mobile.
tasks.v5.6: Same session, immediately after: Gene said v5.5's offset ('-0.233,-0.317' ratio) visibly distorted the nested-arc composition he'd just approved - 'orbits are broken, revert to just now, only a SLIGHT up-left nudge' - plus wanted the whole system faster (not just a wider inner/outer ratio). Dialed DISC_OFFSET_RATIO down to {x:-0.06,y:-0.09} (about a quarter of v5.5's), and raised the base speed coefficient 0.9->1.7 (keeps the a^-2.3 differential exponent from v5.4, just scales overall pace). Screenshot-confirmed the composition reads like the pre-offset version again with only a subtle recentring, and planet movement between successive screenshots (~1.8s apart) is clearly larger than before.
tasks.v5.7: Same session, next round: Gene asked to be able to tune the scene himself instead of round-tripping through Claude, and reported the background starfield clumping into one blob on mobile. Two independent changes: (1) EVERY scene-level constant hand-tuned so far (elevationDeg, rollDeg, focusDistance, fov, offsetXRatio, offsetYRatio, speedCoeff, speedExp, plus a new orbitScale multiplier applied to every orbit's a/size at use-time) moved from module-level consts to an `OrbitalSystemTuning` prop object with defaults (`ORBITAL_SYSTEM_DEFAULTS`). That type+defaults live in a NEW tiny file, src/components/orbitalSystemTuning.ts, with zero imports - critically NOT inside OrbitalSystem.tsx itself, because OrbitalSystem.tsx imports three.js and HeroSection needs to import the tuning type/defaults statically (for useState); a static import from a file that also gets dynamically import()'d elsewhere makes bundlers fold the whole module into the eagerly-loaded chunk, which would have defeated the entire 'three.js loads lazily after first paint' optimisation. Verified with `npm run build`: OrbitalSystem chunk 7KB (up from 3.3KB, expected - more code), three.module still a separate 589KB chunk, main index chunk barely moved (660.65KB -> 661.05KB). Added src/components/HeroTuningPanel.tsx: a fixed-position slider panel (one range input per tuning key, live value readout, Reset, and a 'Copy values' button that writes a ready-to-paste ORBITAL_SYSTEM_DEFAULTS object literal to the clipboard) rendered only via `const HeroTuningPanel = import.meta.env.DEV ? lazy(...) : null` in HeroSection - Vite statically replaces import.meta.env.DEV with false in production, so both the lazy() call and the panel are dead-code-eliminated from the prod build (confirmed: no HeroTuningPanel chunk in the build output, prod bundle size unaffected). The effect's dependency array lists each tuning value as an individual primitive (not the merged `{...DEFAULTS, ...props}` object, which is a fresh reference every render) so unrelated re-renders (e.g. the hero's typewriter ticking every ~50ms) don't tear down and rebuild the WebGL scene - only an actual slider drag does. Puppeteer-verified: focusing a slider and pressing ArrowRight 10x moved its value 14->24 with no console errors. (2) Star-clump root cause found in ParticleNetwork.tsx (the DOM connecting-dots layer, not the WebGL star Points): particles were seeded ONCE at mount using canvas.offsetWidth/Height, with only a bare `window.addEventListener('resize', ...)` that resized the canvas BUFFER but never re-seeded or rescaled particle positions. The hero's minHeight is 'auto' below the md breakpoint, so the section's real height depends on settled text/photo layout - on mobile the first measurement could be too small (or the DevTools/orientation switch never fires a window resize at all), leaving all 80 particles clumped in whatever tiny box they first spawned into, with only weak damped repulsion (max speed 1.4px/frame) to ever separate them. Fixed by replacing the one-shot resize+listener with a ResizeObserver on the canvas itself (catches container/layout-driven size changes, not just window resize) that seeds particles on first real measurement and, on subsequent size changes, rescales existing particles proportionally (x *= newW/oldW, y *= newH/oldH) instead of leaving them in place - smooth continuity across breakpoint switches instead of a clump or a jarring reshuffle.
tasks.v5.8: Same session, Gene pasted his own hand-tuned values from the panel's Copy button (elevationDeg 13, rollDeg -25, focusDistance 7.1, fov 50, offsetXRatio -0.25, offsetYRatio -0.12, speedCoeff 2.6, speedExp 1.8, orbitScale 1) - these are now ORBITAL_SYSTEM_DEFAULTS in orbitalSystemTuning.ts, replacing every prior Claude-guessed default (kept as the file's only value block, with a comment noting Gene chose these directly). Also added a collapse/expand toggle to HeroTuningPanel (Gene: wants to see the full scene sometimes while still in dev) - collapses to a small fixed IconButton (TuneIcon) in the same top-right spot, expands back via ChevronRight in the panel header; collapsed state persisted to localStorage (try/catch-wrapped, falls back to expanded) so it survives a dev-server reload. Puppeteer-verified the full cycle: expanded -> collapse -> reload (still collapsed) -> expand, no console errors.
tasks.v5.9: Same session, Gene: applied one more manual tweak (offsetXRatio -0.25 -> -0.21, now the only ORBITAL_SYSTEM_DEFAULTS), reported the background starfield STILL looked wrong on mobile despite v5.7's seeding fix, and asked whether mobile's orbit composition can be tuned separately from desktop's. Two changes: (1) The real starfield bug was density, not seeding - src/components/ParticleNetwork.tsx used a FIXED PARTICLE_COUNT=80 regardless of canvas size; the mobile hero's canvas area is roughly a quarter of desktop's (minHeight:auto, narrow viewport), so the same 80 particles packed into a quarter of the space read about 4x denser, and with a fixed CONNECT_DIST=100px nearly everything linked into one dense tangle instead of a sparse network - that dense tangle IS what read as 'a clump'. Fixed by making count scale with canvas area (PARTICLE_DENSITY_REF: 80 particles per 1440x900, clamped 20-100) instead of a fixed number; seedOrRescale now reseeds (not rescales) whenever the target count for the current size differs from the current particle count. (2) Added a real per-breakpoint tuning profile: orbitalSystemTuning.ts now also exports ORBITAL_SYSTEM_MOBILE_OVERRIDES (a Partial<OrbitalSystemTuning>, empty by default so mobile just inherits desktop's look until tuned). HeroSection holds separate desktopTuning/mobileTuning state and picks which one is active via useMediaQuery('(max-width:899px)') - critically, WHICHEVER breakpoint you're actually viewing is the one the panel edits (no manual toggle needed): drag a slider above 900px and it's editing/saving-shape for ORBITAL_SYSTEM_DEFAULTS, narrow the window below 900px (or use DevTools device mode) and the exact same panel now edits ORBITAL_SYSTEM_MOBILE_OVERRIDES instead. HeroTuningPanel gained a `profile` prop that (a) labels the header 'Editing: Desktop (>=900px)' / 'Editing: Mobile (<900px)' so it's never ambiguous which profile is live, (b) picks the right variable name in the Copy-values snippet, and (c) a `resetValue` prop (replacing a hardcoded ORBITAL_SYSTEM_DEFAULTS import) so Reset goes back to whichever profile's own saved baseline, not always desktop's. Screenshot-verified both profile labels render correctly at their respective viewport widths.
tasks.v5.10: Same session, AFTER v5.9 was committed (d77e813/ebd1cb1): Gene noticed the hero scene has a hard bottom edge - clipped exactly at the section boundary instead of feeling truly full-bleed - and asked for the parts dipping into the next section to gradually fade instead. Removed `overflow: 'hidden'` from Hero's own Box (both background-layer wrappers are position:absolute, so this doesn't affect scroll-snap height math - absolutely positioned content is taken out of flow) - NOT split into overflowX:hidden/overflowY:visible, because browsers force the 'visible' axis to behave as 'auto' when the other axis differs, which would have made Hero an independently-scrollable region. Both the ParticleNetwork starfield (now wrapped in its own positioned Box, previously a bare canvas) and the OrbitalSystem host Box extend BLEED px past Hero's own bottom edge (xs:90, md:200) via a negative `bottom` override sitting after the `inset:0` shorthand in the same sx object (longhand-after-shorthand override, standard CSS cascade - verified with getComputedStyle rather than assumed), with a CSS mask-image fading them to fully transparent well before the end of that extension. Both wrappers' zIndex was bumped from 0 to 1 - required because AboutSection (the next section) has no explicit z-index (computed 'auto'), and per CSS stacking rules z-index:auto/0 positioned siblings paint in DOM order (AboutSection, being LATER in the DOM, would otherwise paint OVER Hero's bleeding content) while any explicit z-index>0 lifts an element into a higher paint layer regardless of DOM order - zIndex:1 on the bleed wrappers (tied with the Container's existing zIndex:1, whose later DOM position still wins that tie so hero's own text stays on top) was enough to beat AboutSection's auto/0 layer. Caught and fixed a real math bug before declaring this done: the first version's fade-end mask stop used `calc(100% - (bleed-20)px)`, which reaches full transparency only 20px into the bleed regardless of bleed size (verified via getComputedStyle + a scrolled screenshot showing full-opacity stars still visible behind the About heading) - the working fade-end stop is a FIXED `calc(100% - 20px)` (20px before the very bottom of the extended box), giving a long ~250px gradual dissolve across most of the bleed instead of an abrupt one right at the seam. Verified on BOTH desktop and mobile (getComputedStyle confirmed bottom/height/maskImage scale correctly per breakpoint) across multiple scroll depths through the transition zone: the dissolve is smooth and fully resolved before About's heading, and the normal (unscrolled) hero view is pixel-identical to before.
tasks.v5.11: Same session, immediately after: Gene asked whether the bleed/fade effect also applies on mobile (yes - confirmed again explicitly with a dedicated mobile getComputedStyle + scrolled screenshot check, not just inferred from the responsive BLEED object) and pasted a further desktop tuning tweak: elevationDeg 13->18, offsetXRatio -0.21->-0.19, offsetYRatio -0.12->-0.15 (rollDeg/focusDistance/fov/speedCoeff/speedExp/orbitScale unchanged). Mobile overrides (from v5.9's round) untouched.

projectsShowcaseOptions.trigger: Gene flagged that the current per-project presentation in ProjectsSection.tsx feels generic and asked whether ThreeUI has a more suitable reference pattern.

currentImplementation.pattern: Filterable 2-column CSS-grid of tiles (16:10 screenshot, hover-scale image, title/tagline/role/facts) + grid/list view toggle, click opens a MUI Dialog with the full write-up and link buttons.
currentImplementation.assessment: Functionally solid and already data-driven (one catalogue array feeds tile, list row, and dialog), but the visual pattern itself - screenshot card grid opening a modal - is a very common SaaS/portfolio convention, which is what reads as generic rather than any execution flaw.
currentImplementation.alreadyPlannedButNotShipped: site-audit-2026-09-15.json projectsPlan.layout already calls for the first featured project to span full width on desktop for hierarchy; current grid is still a uniform repeat(2, 1fr) - this is a low-effort win independent of any ThreeUI decision.

candidatesReviewed.name: bookshelf
candidatesReviewed.concept: A fully interactive 3D bookshelf: each item is a book with its own cover, clicking opens it into a paged detail view (browse UI, prev/next, inspect, open/close book, page-turn controls, a selection counter and palette label all wired up).
candidatesReviewed.fitToAsk: Conceptually the closest match to 'a better way to browse a list of discrete works' of everything in the library - books-as-projects, page-turning as the detail view.
candidatesReviewed.effortAndRisk: By far the heaviest option (863KB hand-built renderer, fully bespoke geometry/interaction for book objects specifically). Adapting it to arbitrary project screenshots means rebuilding the book-cover/page system, not swapping assets into an existing template. Also a tone risk: the portfolio's positioning is software/AI/trading-systems engineering credibility (per site-audit-2026-09-15.json decisions), and a literal 3D bookshelf skews toward a design-showpiece feel that could undercut that, the same mismatch flagged for Sylva's forest scene.
candidatesReviewed.verdict: Worth studying as inspiration for the DETAIL view only (e.g. a richer slide-over/page-like transition replacing the current MUI Dialog), not worth adopting as the whole browsing metaphor.

candidatesReviewed.name: character-carousel
candidatesReviewed.files: CharacterCarousel.tsx (6.3KB) + two self-contained HTML sources (filmstrip, wave variants)
candidatesReviewed.concept: A horizontal carousel of item cards. 'Filmstrip' reads as a scroll/drag band of cards with parallax and a focused/scaled current item; 'wave' undulates the row. Mounted via sandboxed iframe with postMessage-driven speed/scale/pause controls, IntersectionObserver + tab-visibility pausing already built in - same lightweight pattern as liquid-form/liquid-metal-button (no three.js dependency confirmed).
candidatesReviewed.fitToAsk: Good reference for elevating the interaction language (focused item scales up, neighbors recede, smooth drag/scroll-snap) without changing what's fundamentally a card-based browse - closer to an incremental upgrade than a rebuild.
candidatesReviewed.effortAndRisk: Low-medium. The architecture (iframe isolation, visibility-based pausing, postMessage controls) is directly reusable even if built as a native DOM component instead of copying their HTML/CSS verbatim (project cards need real links/accessibility, which a sandboxed iframe complicates - would recommend reimplementing the interaction natively in React rather than reusing their iframe approach for this one).
candidatesReviewed.verdict: Best proportional upgrade candidate: keep the current data model and dialog, replace the static grid's motion language with a filmstrip-style focused-card interaction on desktop, keep simple stacked cards or horizontal snap on mobile (audit's projectsPlan.layout already asks for horizontal snap on mobile).

candidatesReviewed.name: gallery
candidatesReviewed.concept: A rotating cylindrical wall of images (CoverFlow-like), texture-mapped project screenshots on curved panels, auto-rotating with a slow vertical bob.
candidatesReviewed.fitToAsk: Visually striking but decorative/ambient by nature - built for passive display (role=img, aria-hidden canvas), not for click-through to a detail view with metadata, filtering, and multiple links per item, which the projects section needs.
candidatesReviewed.effortAndRisk: Low to build (small, self-contained, real three.js so no iframe complexity) but wrong shape for the actual requirement - would work as a decorative header strip above the real project list, not as a replacement for it.
candidatesReviewed.verdict: Not a fit for the primary showcase; only worth considering later as a small decorative accent (e.g. a rotating strip of screenshots above the section heading), and only if it doesn't conflict with the Sylva-plan's mobile GPU/battery risk budget above.

implementation.history: v1 (2026-09-16 am): unboxed editorial tiles on a snap track, only scale 0.84-1 + opacity separated the centred card. Gene rejected it: 'boring while sliding, current card not highlighted, eyebrow text too small, the old bordered/tilt track (commit 7a43e38) was better'. v2 (same day) replaced the tile with StageCard.
implementation.what: Desktop (>=900px) 'cards' view = Filmstrip of StageCard glass cards on a horizontal scroll-snap track. Per card, framer-motion useScroll({ container, target, axis: 'x', layoutEffect: false }) drives: active (0->1->0 over progress 0.3-0.7), scale 0.84-1, CoverFlow rotateY -18..0..18deg, filter grayscale 0.75->0 / brightness 0.5->1, an ambient-light layer (the card's own screenshot blurred 48px behind the glass, opacity=active), and a breathing accent ring (opacity=active). Centred card gets pointer tilt (spring rotateX/rotateY) + a pointer-following specular sheen (mix-blend screen). Card: 20px radius, dark smoked glass rgba(11,15,24,0.78) fill (a light rgba(255,255,255,0.05) fill was tried first and light screenshots like VCDF/Britween blew the body out to near-white, making the title unreadable; the ambient glow is likewise capped at opacity 0.55 + brightness(0.8) for the same reason), backdrop-filter blur(22px) saturate(160%), 1px glass stroke, org/year as glass pills over the screenshot (0.8rem mono - the fix for the 'too small eyebrow' complaint), title 1.7-1.9rem, tagline 1.02rem, facts as accent chips. Clicking a receded neighbour centres it; clicking the centred card opens the Dialog. Counter '02 / 11' + track-progress bar + active title under the track. Section background gets the centred card's screenshot as a blur(90px) colour wash (AnimatePresence crossfade, opacity 0.22). Card width per breakpoint via CARD_W ({xs:'clamp(240px,78vw,380px)', sm:'clamp(380px,55vw,460px)', md:'clamp(380px,40vw,500px)'}), media 16:9, track items vertically centred (Gene asked for a shorter section / smaller cards after v2; section py md 7). Prev/Next glass buttons auto-hide at the ends; ArrowLeft/Right step; :focus-visible cards are centred. role=region/aria-roledescription=carousel + per-slide labels. List view and Dialog untouched. v3 (2026-09-16, same day): Gene noticed mobile wasn't swiping - the desktop-only Filmstrip had a >=900px gate that fell back to a plain vertical Tile stack on mobile, contradicting site-audit-2026-09-15.json projectsPlan.layout ('keep horizontal snap row on mobile'). Removed the isDesktop gate entirely (Filmstrip now renders at every width via the responsive CARD_W above) and deleted the now-fully-dead Tile/Meta components (~140 lines) rather than leave them unused. Added xs padding/font-size to StageCard's content block, which had only md-value spacing/typography (mobile was getting zero padding + the default oversized h4). Verified with a real Puppeteer touchscreen swipe on a 390px viewport: scrollLeft moved 0->328 and correctly centred the next card.
implementation.gotcha: framer-motion useScroll defaults to a layout effect; a child's layout effect runs BEFORE the parent track's ref is attached, so container resolved to null -> document and nothing ever updated after scrolling (v2 shipped that bug for ~10 min). layoutEffect: false fixes it. Keep it on every useScroll whose container/target ref belongs to an ancestor.
implementation.verified: Headless Chrome 1440x900: after Next, centred card filter grayscale(0)/brightness(1), glow opacity 1, neighbours grayscale(0.75)/0.5; counter 02/11 -> 03/11; neighbour click centres without opening the dialog; centred click opens the Dialog with the right title; hover tilt applies; no console errors. tsc clean.
implementation.deliberatelySkipped: Vertical-wheel hijack (traps page scrolling on a single-page site), mouse drag-to-scroll (click-vs-drag threshold), three.js/WebGL materials (CSS 3D + blur gets the look at a fraction of the GPU cost; revisit only after the hero-scene decision).
implementation.tunables: In StageCard: active window (0.3-0.7), turn angle (+-18), grayscale/brightness floors (0.75/0.5), glow blur (48px), ring shadow; FILMSTRIP_CARD_W; wash opacity (0.22) and blur (90px) in ProjectsSection; arrow top offset (30%).

recommendation.notRecommended: Do not adopt the bookshelf's full 3D shelf metaphor or the gallery's rotating cylinder as the primary showcase mechanism - both read as visual showpieces that work against the engineering-credibility positioning, mirroring the tone concern already raised about Sylva's forest scene.
